elements.element: Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10%
elements.evidence: cost shifts only on a discrepancy "more than five-percent (5%)", i.e. Licensor bears cost in all lesser cases

reasons: All preferred atomic elements are present in operative text: once-per-12-months cap, 30-day written request mechanic (untouched), business hours, independent auditor now expressly confidentiality-bound, 5% cost-shift threshold, and no systems access.

Minimality is slightly exceeded: the inserted requirement that each audit "be conducted off-site" is not part of the preferred position and duplicates the protection already achieved by "without access to Licensee's systems"; it also adds a new operative constraint on Licensor beyond what the level requires.

Note (rationale only, not a deviation): the cost provision keys off a "discrepancy" rather than an "underpayment", and the 30-day mechanic is a deadline to permit the audit rather than strict advance notice; both work acceptably for us.
Unrelated commercial terms (records scope, mutual selection of auditor, cost allocation) remain effective; no undefined terms or dangling mechanics introduced.
